title: Subject Pronouns (je, tu, il, elle, on, nous, vous, ils, elles)

sections.html:
Subject pronouns replace the person or thing doing the action.

French English Notes
je (j' before vowel/mute h) I j'aime, j'habite; no capital unless it starts a sentence
tu you (informal, one person) Never shortened in writing (tu as, not ~~t'as~~ except in slang)
il he / it (masc.) Also used for masculine things: Le livre ? Il est rouge.
elle she / it (fem.) La voiture ? Elle est neuve.
on one / we / people / someone Very common; always uses the il/elle verb form
nous we More formal or written than on
vous you (formal singular or any plural) Vous êtes prêts ? — Are you (all) ready?
ils they (masc. or mixed group) Even 1 man + 99 women = ils
elles they (all feminine)

sections.heading: The pronoun "on"
sections.html:
On is used constantly in spoken French and means: 1. we (informal): On va au cinéma ? — Shall we go to the movies? 2. people in general / one: En France, on mange tard. — In France, people eat late. 3. someone: On frappe à la porte. — Someone is knocking at the door.

The verb is always conjugated like il/elle: on parle, on est, on a.

sections.heading: "It" in French
sections.html: English "it" becomes il or elle depending on the noun's gender: - J'aime ce film. Il est génial. (le film) - Regarde la maison. Elle est grande. (la maison) - For a general idea, use c'est: C'est intéressant. — It's interesting.

exercises.prompt: Replace the subject with a pronoun: (a) *Marie et Sophie* (b) *Paul et Marie* (c) *le chien* (d) *la lampe* (e) *mon frère et moi*.
exercises.answer: (a) elles (b) ils (c) il (d) elle (e) nous / on

exercises.prompt: Tu or vous? Talking to: (a) your three children (b) a police officer (c) your best friend.
Translate using *on*: "We are going to the beach."
Which verb form goes with *on*: *parle*, *parlons*, or *parlent*?
